doing filesystem work outside an anchor, and the diagnostic that would surface the
condition they now refuse. This brings them onto the same footing as the rest of
the tree.

## Pi's extension directory

`agent/pi/hooks.go` was the last registered agent whose hook-config surface had
not moved. It joined `.pi/extensions/entire/index.ts` onto the repo root and
handed the result to `os.ReadFile` / `os.MkdirAll` / `os.WriteFile` /
`os.RemoveAll`, each with a `//nolint:gosec` about where the path was *built*
rather than where it *resolves* — the justification `agent.HookConfigFile`'s doc
comment already calls out as the one that says nothing useful. A working tree
arrives by clone, so `.pi` is a component the repository supplies, and every one
of those four calls resolved through it.

Routed through `agent.OpenHookConfig`, which the other eight agents already use:
the base is the worktree root, `.pi/extensions/entire/index.ts` is a name inside

(`DetectPresence` stats `.pi`), so it reaches these operations without the user
naming it, which is the argument for routing a new agent through the anchor by
default rather than trusting review to notice.

Two supporting pieces:

- **`osroot.RemoveAllNoSymlinks`.** `os.Root.RemoveAll` refuses a descent that
  would leave the root and unlinks a symlinked leaf rather than following it, but

content.text: All 13 findings verified against the code (one empirically with a Go repro).

findings.short_summary: os.Root refuses absolute in-repo vercel.json symlinks
findings.summary: Moving Vercel detection behind os.Root breaks the exact monorepo setup its own comment says it preserves: os.Root refuses an ABSOLUTE symlink target unconditionally, even one resolving inside the root.
findings.failure_scenario: Verified with a Go 1.26.6 repro: for `vercel.json -> /abs/path/inside/repo/shared/vercel.json`, `root.Stat("vercel.json")` returns `statat vercel.json: path escapes from parent` and `os.IsNotExist(err)` is false, while plain `os.Stat` succeeds. A relative link (`shared/vercel.json`) passes. So `entire enable` on such a repo now prints `Note: Skipping Vercel deployment update: could not check vercel.json: statat vercel.json: path escapes from parent` and returns `false, nil`, silently dropping the feature it used to offer. Same for `.vercel` / `vercel.ts` (setup.go:2333) and for `vercelconfig.LoadIn` (vercelconfig.go:88), whose doc claims "a symlink that stays inside the repository is still followed" — true only for relative links. CLAUDE.md already records this exact os.Root property as the reason checkpoint/configloader.go keeps a symlink-following billy.Basic.

findings.short_summary: Wrong-typed component reported as NOT READABLE
findings.summary: scanForSymlinkedComponent funnels every non-ENOENT stat error into componentScanUnreadable, so a wrong-typed component gets the "NOT READABLE" heading and an ownership/permissions remedy that cannot fix it.
findings.failure_scenario: Put a regular file at `.claude`. The walk Lstats `.claude` (fine, not a symlink), then `.claude/settings.json` returns ENOTDIR — not ENOENT — so doctor prints `Agent config directories: NOT READABLE` / `.claude/settings.json` / `Fix: check the ownership and permissions of each path above.` The actual fix is "remove the file at .claude". This is the else-branch pattern CLAUDE.md's `.entire` section forbids by name: it separates ErrEntireDirNotDirectory from ErrEntireDirUnreadable precisely because "replace the path" and "fix ownership" are different remedies, and says an unmatched error gets NO remedy.

findings.short_summary: .claude/agents/ missing from doctor's candidate list
findings.summary: `.claude/agents/` is absent from agentSymlinkCheckPaths even though Entire deletes through it, so a symlink there produces exactly the silent failure this check exists to surface.
findings.failure_scenario: Dumped the live candidate list by calling agentSymlinkCheckPaths() in-process: 19 paths, and none is under `.claude/agents`. `.codex/agents/entire.toml` and `.gemini/agents/entire.md` are covered, but only incidentally via agentHelpSkillTemplate. Meanwhile removeLegacySearchSubagent (setup_search_skill.go:93,116) deletes `.claude/agents/entire-search.md` through osroot.LstatNoSymlinks, which refuses a symlinked parent — its own doc says "That matters because .claude/agents/ arrives with a checkout". With `.claude/agents` symlinked, enable emits a best-effort LegacyCleanupWarning and `entire doctor` says nothing at all.

findings.short_summary: RemoveDir guards only the worktree root, not agent roots
findings.summary: RemoveDir refuses only `dir == "."`, so for every agent except pi it would recursively delete the agent's own top-level directory — the outcome its doc says must not happen, with nothing enforcing it.
findings.failure_scenario: `path.Dir(f.name)` is `.claude` for `.claude/settings.json`, `.cursor` for `.cursor/hooks.json`, `.codex` for `.codex/hooks.json`. The doc comment states "taking the parent would delete the user's own config with it", but the only guard is the worktree-root check. Any future caller — or a copy-paste during the next agent integration, which this PR shows is the live pattern — gets `RemoveAll(".claude")` on uninstall, wiping the user's hand-written settings, subagents and skills. The rest of the PR argues for making exactly this kind of precondition structural (see the build guard added for HookConfigLocator); rejecting a target that is itself an AllProtectedDirs() entry would do it.

findings.short_summary: Build guard compares counts, not sets
findings.summary: The new build guard asserts `len(declared) == len(callers)`, so it passes whenever an added omission is offset by a removal, and reds the build on package layouts it does not intend to reject.
findings.failure_scenario: Add agent X that calls agent.OpenHookConfig without implementing HookConfigLocator while any existing locator is dropped in the same change: counts still match, the guard passes, and doctor silently loses coverage — the precise failure the test's own doc calls "invisible at the call site". Conversely, an agent whose OpenHookConfig call sits in a sub-package (`agent/foo/internal/...`) counts as two callers for one declared path and fails the build with no defect present. Comparing the set of caller package basenames against the set of declared top-level directories is what the doc claims is happening.

findings.short_summary: Pi extension dir perms silently drop 0755 -> 0750
findings.summary: Routing pi through HookConfigFile.Write changes its extension directory permissions from 0755 to 0750, dropping the rationale the deleted code carried.
findings.failure_scenario: The removed lines were `os.MkdirAll(filepath.Dir(path), 0o755)` with `//nolint:gosec // G301: pi reads the directory; standard 0755 permissions`. HookConfigFile.Write hardcodes `osroot.MkdirAllNoSymlink(f.root, dir, 0o750)` (hook_config_file.go:130) for every component it creates — `.pi`, `.pi/extensions`, `.pi/extensions/entire`. Where `entire enable` runs as a different uid/gid than the pi process (devcontainer with root setup and a `node` agent, sandboxed CI runner), pi can no longer traverse the directory and the extension stops loading — and pi's fireHook swallows every error by design, so it fails silently. The replacement comment mentions only the 0644 file mode.

findings.short_summary: checkAgentDirSymlinks returns silently when OpenAt fails
findings.summary: checkAgentDirSymlinks bare-returns when worktreedir.OpenAt fails, contradicting the "we could not find out is not there is nothing here" stance the same function applies twelve lines later to individual components.
findings.failure_scenario: `root, err := worktreedir.OpenAt(worktreeRoot); if err != nil { return }` — no message. osroot.Shared fails on a worktree root that is unreadable or has been replaced, which is precisely a state where every hook install will also fail. Doctor then prints nothing for this section, reporting a clean bill of health on a repo where nothing can be installed. The per-component path deliberately surfaces the same condition as NOT READABLE, with a comment explaining why swallowing it is wrong.

findings.short_summary: .github/.agents flagged for agents that were never enabled
findings.summary: Candidates are not gated on the agent actually being configured, so `.github` and `.agents` — user-owned directories Entire may have written nothing into — are reported with a `git rm --cached` instruction.
findings.failure_scenario: The dumped candidate list includes `.github/hooks/entire.json`, `.github/skills/entire-search/SKILL.md` and `.agents/skills/entire-search/SKILL.md`. A monorepo that symlinks `.github` (shared workflows) or `.agents` — which setup_search_skill.go:186 itself documents as "a shared, user-authored skills directory" — gets `Agent config directories: SYMLINKS PRESENT` on every `entire doctor` even though Copilot CLI and Codex were never enabled. The function's own doc argues against exactly this ("reporting it would train the user to ignore this section") and excludes `.vogon` on those grounds.

findings.short_summary: VolumeName pairing misses Windows rooted-relative \foo
findings.summary: The new VolumeName pairing closes `C:foo` but leaves the sibling Windows rooted-relative form `\foo`, which still takes the "name inside the worktree" branch.
findings.failure_scenario: On Windows, Go's volumeNameLen is 0 for a single leading backslash (not a volume, not a UNC prefix), so `filepath.IsAbs("\\foo\\bar")` is false AND `filepath.VolumeName("\\foo\\bar")` is "" — the guard passes. Clean+ToSlash yields `/foo/bar`; `paths.IsRelativeTraversal` only tests for a `..` prefix (paths.go:319) so it returns false, and Name answers "yes, inside the worktree" for a drive-rooted path. Same class as the case being fixed, same containment role, same caller (readWorktreeFileSafely, fed API-supplied paths), and — like `C:foo` — not a live escape because os.Root rejects it one layer down. `filepath.IsLocal` is the single primitive covering both, and is what os.Root itself uses. Marked plausible only because I could not execute on Windows; it follows from documented filepath semantics.

findings.short_summary: Two doc comments point at symbols that do not exist
findings.summary: Two doc comments introduced or left by this diff cross-reference deleted or misnamed symbols, and in a tree where these comments are the primary spec that costs the next reader the whole explanation.
findings.failure_scenario: doctor.go:848 says "because firstSymlinkedComponent examines every component of what it is given" — grep finds zero definitions; the function is scanForSymlinkedComponent (doctor.go:913). And hook_config_file.go:191 reads "GeneratedState is GeneratedHookFileState for a file read through this root. See that function for what marker and render mean" — GeneratedHookFileState is deleted by this same PR (grep finds only this comment), so the only place `marker` and `render` were explained is now unreachable from the pointer.

findings.short_summary: readCapped doc says bytes, callers say chars, cuts mid-rune
findings.summary: The rewritten doc comment describes the cap in bytes while the callers' constants are labelled chars, and the truncation still slices at a byte offset.
findings.failure_scenario: `tuneDocCap = 6000 // max chars embedded per doc (CLAUDE.md etc.)` and `tuneReadmeCap = 2000` feed a function that does `s = s[:maxLen] + "\n…(truncated)…"`. A CLAUDE.md whose 6000th byte falls inside a multi-byte rune emits an invalid UTF-8 sequence into the prompt the runner sends to the model. Pre-existing, but the diff re-touches and re-documents both lines; backing up with utf8.DecodeLastRuneInString (or strings.ToValidUTF8 on the slice) is a one-line fix.

findings.short_summary: RemoveAllNoSymlinks double-wraps, naming the dir twice
findings.summary: RemoveAllNoSymlinks wraps its error with the name and HookConfigFile.RemoveDir wraps it again with the absolute path, producing a message that names the same directory twice.
findings.failure_scenario: A symlinked `.pi` yields `remove /repo/.pi/extensions/entire: remove .pi/extensions/entire: .pi: path is a symlink`. RemoveNoSymlinks, immediately above in the same file, deliberately returns `Remove(parent, leaf)` unwrapped so its one caller owns the naming — RemoveAllNoSymlinks should match it, or RemoveDir should stop re-wrapping.

findings.short_summary: Skill template bodies built then discarded on every doctor run
findings.summary: agentSymlinkCheckPaths materializes every skill-template body just to read the path beside it, then discards the bytes.
findings.failure_scenario: searchSkillTemplate and agentHelpSkillTemplate return `(relPath, content, ok)` where content is `[]byte(strings.TrimSpace(<multi-KB template>) + "\n")`; the caller binds it to `_`. Twelve template bodies are trimmed and copied on every `entire doctor` run to produce nineteen short strings. Splitting the path lookup out (a templatePathFor(agentName) both builders call) removes the allocation and makes the intent — "I want the path, not the file" — legible.

content.text:
**PR #2220 — 13 findings.** Everything is verified against the tree; one with an executed repro.

The one I'd block on:

**`setup.go:2324` / `vercelconfig.go:88` — the anchor breaks the setup its own comment promises to keep.** Both doc comments say an in-repo symlink is still followed. That's only true for *relative* links. `os.Root` refuses an absolute target unconditionally, even one landing inside the root — I confirmed it on Go 1.26.6:

```
root.Stat("vercel.json")      err=statat vercel.json: path escapes from parent  IsNotExist=false
os.Stat  (vercel.json)        err=<nil>
root.Stat("vercel-rel.json")  err=<nil>
```

Because `os.IsNotExist` is false, `entire enable` takes the error branch, prints `Note: Skipping Vercel deployment update: could not check vercel.json: … path escapes from parent`, and returns `false, nil` — the feature silently disappears for a repo where it used to work. Same for `.vercel`/`vercel.ts`. CLAUDE.md already records this exact `os.Root` property as why `checkpoint/configloader.go` keeps a symlink-following `billy.Basic`, so the precedent for handling it is in-tree.

Three more where the code and its own documentation disagree:

- **`doctor.go:922`** — a regular file at `.claude` yields ENOTDIR, which funnels into `componentScanUnreadable`, so doctor prints `NOT READABLE` with a permissions remedy for a problem only `rm .claude` fixes. This is the `else`-branch pattern CLAUDE.md's `.entire` section forbids by name.

---
name: trail-write-gotchas
description: "entire trail write gotchas: the body has its own PUT route (the old PATCH 503 was a wrong-route bug), labels are not writable, and probing safely needs a scratch trail with a branch"
metadata:
  type: reference
---

Gotchas when exercising `entire trail` **writes** against entire-api.

There is no backend switch to set: `ENTIRE_TRAILS_BACKEND` was removed on
2026-08-18 and entire-api is the only backend, so writes work by default. (The
old advice to export that var is dead — don't go looking for it.)

- **A trail's description is written by `PUT .../trails/{host}/{owner}/{repo}/{number}/body`, never by the trail PATCH.**
  The PATCH route answers a `body` field with an unconditional 503, and the API
  redacts 5xx messages, so the caller sees a bare "Service Unavailable" — which
  is why the earlier probe (2026-08-17, trail #1017, 200 B–4 KB, retried over
  ~10 minutes) read as a flaky server or a size limit. It was neither: wrong
  route. Fixed in the CLI on 2026-08-19 (`sendTrailBody` in `trail_cmd.go`);
  `api.TrailUpdateRequest` deliberately has no `Body` field so the mistake
  cannot be re-made. The PUT takes `{markdown, overwrite}` (or `contentJson`
  instead of `markdown`) and **refuses a non-empty description with 409
  `document_not_empty` unless `overwrite: true`** — that flag is what makes
  editing an existing description work at all. Its `If-Match` alternative is
  unusable from a read: the ETag comes only from this route's own response
  header, and `bodyDocument.updatedAt` from a trail read is formatted to a
  different precision, so a reconstructed header never matches.
- **Labels are read-only.** `--add-label`/`--remove-label` no longer exist; the
  API accepts no label writes. Reads (`trail show`'s `Labels:` line) still work.
- **Probing safely needs a scratch trail *with* a branch.** `trail update` can
  only target a trail **by branch**, so a `--no-branch` scratch trail is
  unpatchable — but creating one with `--branch` also **creates and pushes that
  branch to origin**. Clean up both the trail and the remote branch afterwards.

description: "Keep trail findings, PR comments and review write-ups short; no self-justifying prose"
metadata:

Stefan, on trail findings I posted 2-4x longer than my chat summary of the same
points (2026-08-13, trail #1039): "why are the findings so much longer than what
you wrote me here?" then "don't add so much fluff, nobody reads that either".
Trimmed 113-271 words down to 26-106 and that was the right length.

**Why:** a finding is read cold by the owner who then decides. It does not need
to sell itself, and length actively costs readership — the padding makes the
mechanism harder to find, not better supported.

**How to apply:** in findings, PR comments and review write-ups, keep the
mechanism, the `file:line` of any second occurrence, the suggested diff, and one
line of verification evidence. Cut:

- topic sentences that argue for the finding's own importance ("The failure mode
  is what makes this worth a line of insurance rather than a shrug")
- meta-commentary on my own severity or stance ("Flagging for the future, not
  asking for a change here — I think leaving this alone is the right call")
- "Worth fixing because…" framing on nits — a stale comment gets one sentence
- explaining the same mechanism both before and after a code block

The tell is a finding that opens by justifying itself. Severity and location
already do that job. Do not expand a chat-length point when writing it to a
durable artifact; the cold reader needs *context* (the second file, the repro),
not *persuasion*.

Related: [[deslop-unwired-functions]].

way.

All 13 fixed and pushed to PR #2220 as five commits. `mise run lint` and `mise run test:ci` both exit 0 on the committed state; CI is running and I'm watching it.

**The real bug** was the vercel one, and fixing it turned up a second I'd missed. `worktreeFileName` now resolves through `NameFollowingLinks` when the root refuses with something other than "absent", so an absolute in-repo link is followed and one leaving the worktree still isn't. Writing the test exposed that resolving only the *target* is wrong: on macOS `/var` → `/private/var`, so every repo under a symlinked path judged its own files as outside itself. The base needs resolving against the same rules — that was my bug, caught by the test, not the review.

**Two I decided rather than changed**, both recorded in the code:

- **pi's `0755` → `0750`** — kept at `0750`. The other eight agents have been on it all along and pi runs as whoever ran `entire enable`; a differing-uid setup breaks all nine equally and isn't pi's to fix here. The silent part was the missing note, so the note is what I added.
- **`.github`/`.agents` noise** — staying noisy per your call, with the reasoning in the doc comment: gating would have to ask whether hooks are installed, and that reads through the very config a symlink hides, so the check would go silent exactly where it's needed.

**One finding I think is wrong** — and it's Paulo's, not mine. His `01M1EY52EGAB` says `RemoveDir` mixes separators between `path.Dir(f.name)` and `filepath.Dir(f.path)`. But only `filepath.Dir(f.path)` reaches the message, and on an OS path that's the correct call — there's no mixing. I left it open for him. Looking there did turn up a genuine one a few lines up, though: `Write` passed `f.path` to `path.Dir`, which on Windows finds no forward slashes and yields `"."`, so the error named the wrong thing. Fixed.

New test coverage: `NameFollowingLinks` (absolute/relative/escaping/dangling), `worktreeFileName`, `componentScanWrongType` and its remedy text, `.claude/agents` coverage, `RemoveDir`'s three cases, and `readCapped` — which had none. I checked the guard test isn't vacuous: both greps find the same eight packages, so dropping one side fails it.

The 13 trail findings are resolved with the commit each landed in.

CI on the first push came back green — all 12 GitHub checks including `test-windows`. The "Entire Gates" failure is only the `approvals` gate (needs a human reviewer); `checks` and `findings` both passed.

The gate did surface three fresh findings from an agent review of my commits, and **one was a real bug I introduced**:

My rune-boundary fix scanned back for a valid UTF-8 prefix with no floor. On a doc that isn't UTF-8 at all — a latin-1 README — every prefix is invalid and `""` is valid, so it walked to zero. Probed it:

```
readCapped(latin-1 CLAUDE.md, cap=20) = "\n…(truncated)…"
```

All content gone, worse than the behaviour I was fixing, and O(maxLen²) getting there. Now bounded to `UTFMax-1` bytes — the most a partial trailing rune can be short — so invalidity my cut didn't cause passes through, matching what the under-cap path already does. My original test used valid multi-byte input and sailed past it.

Chasing that turned up **a second bug in my own test**. Stress-running revealed `TestReadCapped` failing only when run alongside `TestScanForSymlinkedComponent` — which I'd written as `t.Parallel()` *and* with `t.Cleanup(osroot.ResetShared)`, copied from the neighbouring tests. That registry is process-global, so the cleanup closed roots under any concurrent test. The neighbours get away with it because they're serial (`t.Chdir`). Dropped it; a unique temp dir needs no cleanup. That's a live landmine for any parallel test in the package.

One I pushed back on: the third finding repeated Paulo's `01M1EY52EGAB` claim about mixed separators in `RemoveDir`. Dismissed with reasoning — only `filepath.Dir(f.path)` reaches the message and `f.path` is OS-separated throughout. I noted the real separator bug next door that I did fix.

Also worth flagging: my earlier "test:ci exits 0" was from a run where I'd discarded output. A later run exited 1, and re-running went green — so one of those five runs flaked, and I can't say which since the output was gone. Four of five clean, and the touched packages survive `-count=5`. Likely the known macOS codex `/var` local failure, but I didn't prove it.

`osroot.ResetShared()` clears the process-global root registry, so calling it from a `t.Parallel()` test closes roots out from under whatever else is running. The failure surfaces in the *innocent* test, not the one that reset — so it reads as a flake in unrelated code.

Hit on 2026-09-02 (PR #2220): a `t.Parallel` test I added to `doctor_test.go` with `t.Cleanup(osroot.ResetShared)` made `TestReadCapped_*` fail with `readCapped() not ok`, because `readCapped` calls `worktreedir.OpenAt` → `osroot.Shared`. Each test passed alone with `-count=5`; only the combination failed. `go test -count=5 -run 'A|B'` bisecting over pairs is what found it.

**Why:** the 9 existing `ResetShared` callers in `cmd/entire/cli/doctor_test.go` are all serial (they use `t.Chdir`, so they cannot be parallel), which makes the pattern look safe to copy into a parallel test. It is not — this is exactly the "modifies process-global state" exception in CLAUDE.md's always-`t.Parallel()` rule.

**How to apply:** a test that opens a root on its own `t.TempDir()` needs no cleanup at all — a registry entry for a unique temp dir is harmless for the process lifetime. Only reset when a test rebuilds or deletes a directory a root is already cached on, and then keep that test serial. Before adding `ResetShared`, ask whether the test is parallel; if it is, drop the reset rather than the `t.Parallel()`.

Corollary for verification: a single clean `mise run test:ci` does not clear this class. Stress the touched packages with `-count=5` *together*, not one at a time.

`scanForSymlinkedComponent` tested `Type() == 0` for "a regular file where a

hook install fail on it. Now an allowlist of the traversable shapes
(`traversableComponent`), which is what the .entire scan's doc argues for at
length — an allowlist a rejected type can enter by setting an extra bit is not
an allowlist. fs.ModeIrregular stays tolerated: a Windows junction arrives as
bare ModeIrregular and a cloud placeholder directory as ModeDir|ModeIrregular,
and both are traversable.

`RemoveDir` refused an `AllProtectedDirs()` entry, which is a blocklist and
misses the case that matters: that list holds `.opencode` and `.github/hooks`
but not `.opencode/plugins`, `.pi/extensions` or `.github`, so a future agent
whose config sits one level below its root still got
`RemoveAll(".opencode/plugins")` — the user's other plugins. Stated positively
instead: the directory has to be one Entire named. Every agent root and shared

**Duplication.**

`printCappedList` replaces four inline copies of the same capped-list loop in
doctor.go (three added by 761b87d68, one pre-existing in
checkEntireDirSymlinks), so the off-by-one truncation contract is written once.
`testutil.SkipWithoutSymlinks` replaces six copies of the Windows symlink skip

expectation of mine: a RELATIVE in-repo link never reaches the resolve, because

content.text:
Pushed as one cleanup commit. `mise run lint` 0 issues, `test:ci` exit 0, and the touched tests survive `-count=5` run together.

**Two of the four agents found real gaps, not just style — my earlier fixes were unsound:**

- `scanForSymlinkedComponent` tested `Type() == 0`, a blocklist of one. A FIFO, socket, or device node at `.claude` came back **clean** while `os.Root` and every hook install fail on it. Now an allowlist of traversable shapes, which is what the `.entire` scan's doc argues for; `ModeIrregular` stays tolerated so Windows junctions and cloud placeholders still pass.
- `RemoveDir`'s `AllProtectedDirs()` check was a blocklist. The altitude agent caught that, but **its proposed fix — component count ≥ 2 — was also unsound**: I dumped the paths and `.opencode/plugins` is 2 components and absent from that list, so it would still permit deleting the user's other OpenCode plugins. Replaced with the positive invariant: the directory must be one Entire *named*. Every agent root and shared intermediate fails it; pi's `.pi/extensions/entire` passes.

**Duplication collapsed:** `printCappedList` for four copies of the capped-list loop, `testutil.SkipWithoutSymlinks` for six copies of the Windows skip in three wordings, one switch again in `agentHelpSkillTemplate`, and the three `worktreeFileName` tests as one table — which **caught a wrong expectation of mine**: a *relative* in-repo link never reaches the resolve because `os.Root` follows it, so the fast path returns the original name. My separate tests had never asserted that case.

**Waste:** `readCapped` was scanning the whole 6KB prefix up to four times; `utf8.RuneStart` answers the same question from one byte (2081ns → 2ns measured) and removes the fallback branch entirely. Plus the dead `vercelJSONName == ""` back-fill and a redundant not-exist exit.

**Skipped, with reasons:**

The one I want to flag hardest is not a cleanup item at all — the altitude agent found that **this repo's own `AGENTS.md` is a symlink to `CLAUDE.md`**, and `readCapped` opens with `osroot.OpenNoFollow`, so `entire runner tune` silently drops it. Harmless here since `CLAUDE.md` is read anyway, but a repo with only a symlinked `AGENTS.md` loses it. That's a correctness bug in Paulo's `99cef4ae9`, outside `/simplify`'s remit, and worth his call on whether symlinked docs should be read.

Three more left deliberately: moving `worktreeFileName` into `worktreedir` as a first-class "user-owned file" API (right instinct — the next caller won't know to do the two-step — but the anchor's two neighbouring helpers have the *opposite* policy, so it needs a deliberate design call); changing `OpenHookConfig` to take a `HookConfigLocator` so the guard test becomes a compile error (genuinely better, but 9 of Paulo's agent packages); and giving the registry a `ManagedWorktreePaths()` capability. All three are follow-ups, not cleanup.

Follow-up to #2220. These seven commits were pushed to `paulo-goroot-ognib` before it merged, but a force-push to that branch dropped them, so none of it reached `main` — every issue below is still live there. Rebased onto current `main` and re-proposed unchanged, apart from three merge resolutions noted at the end.

The first six came out of reviewing #2220; the seventh is a quality pass over the other six.

## The one that changes behaviour for users today

`entire enable` silently drops Vercel deployment blocking in a repo whose `vercel.json` is an absolute symlink into a monorepo's shared config. `708f78136` moved the detection onto the worktree root and said in two places that in-repo links are still followed. That holds only for *relative* links — `os.Root` refuses an absolute target unconditionally, even one landing inside the root, and the error is not `os.ErrNotExist`:

```
root.Stat("vercel.json")      err=statat vercel.json: path escapes from parent
root.Stat("vercel-rel.json")  err=<nil>
```

So the error branch printed `could not check vercel.json: ... path escapes from parent` and returned false. `worktreeFileName` tries the root first and, on a refusal that is not "absent", resolves through the new `worktreedir.NameFollowingLinks` and retries at the resolved name — following a link that stays inside, refusing one that leaves, with the retried read still going through the root. CLAUDE.md already records this `os.Root` property as why `checkpoint/configloader.go` keeps a symlink-following `billy.Basic`.

## Two guards that were not sound

`RemoveDir` guarded only the worktree root, so `path.Dir(".claude/settings.json")` is `.claude` and the next agent integration to copy pi's uninstall gets `RemoveAll(".claude")` — the user's hand-written settings, subagents and skills. A blocklist of `AllProtectedDirs()` was the obvious fix and is also unsound: that list holds `.opencode` and `.github/hooks` but not `.opencode/plugins`, `.pi/extensions` or `.github`, so an agent whose config sits one level below its root still reaches `RemoveAll(".opencode/plugins")`. Stated positively instead — the directory has to be one Entire named. Every agent root and shared intermediate fails that; pi's `.pi/extensions/entire` passes because Entire created it.

`scanForSymlinkedComponent` tested `Type() == 0`, a blocklist of one, so a FIFO, socket or device node where a directory belongs came back clean and doctor printed nothing — while `os.Root` and every hook install fail on it. Now an allowlist of the traversable shapes, which is what the `.entire` scan's doc argues for at length. `fs.ModeIrregular` stays tolerated: a Windows junction arrives as bare `ModeIrregular` and a cloud placeholder directory as `ModeDir|ModeIrregular`, and both are traversable.

## Diagnosis that named the wrong thing, or nothing

A regular file at `.claude` was reported as `NOT READABLE` with `Fix: check the ownership and permissions` — a remedy that cannot fix it. That is the else-branch pattern CLAUDE.md's `.entire` section separates two error values to avoid; it now gets its own `BROKEN` heading and the replace remedy.

`.claude/agents/` was in no candidate, though `removeLegacySearchSubagent` deletes through it with `osroot.LstatNoSymlinks`, which refuses a symlinked parent. A link there was refused at enable with a best-effort warning and doctor said nothing. `.codex/agents` and `.gemini/agents` were covered only as a side effect of the agent-help template living under them.

A worktree root that would not open returned bare, printing nothing on a repo where every hook install also fails.

## Smaller correctness

`readCapped`'s cap is applied in bytes while the callers' constants say chars, so `s[:maxLen]` could cut a rune in half and put invalid UTF-8 into the prompt the runner sends to a model. It now backs off the continuation bytes at the cut — bounded, so a doc that is not UTF-8 at all keeps its content rather than being reduced to the truncation marker. `utf8.RuneStart` answers this from one byte where validating the prefix walked the whole 6KB.

`Write`'s error message passed `f.path` to `path.Dir`, which finds no forward slashes on Windows and yielded `"."`.

The build guard compared `len(declared) == len(callers)`, so an added omission offset by a removal in the same change passed — the exact failure it exists to catch, since the agent still works and only doctor's diagnosis goes quiet. It compares sets now (eight packages each side).

## Quality pass

`printCappedList` replaces four inline copies of the same capped-list loop; `testutil.SkipWithoutSymlinks` replaces six copies of the Windows symlink skip in three wordings; `agentHelpSkillTemplate` is back to one switch so a fourth agent cannot get a path with no body; the `worktreeFileName` tests are one table. Writing that table caught a wrong expectation of mine — a *relative* in-repo link never reaches the resolve, because `os.Root` follows it, so the fast path returns the original name.

## Merge resolutions worth a look

Three conflicts came from `main` moving under these commits, and all three keep `main`'s side:

- `agent_hook_config_guard_test.go` — `main` added `grep.Env = gitrepo.EnvWithoutRepoOverrides()` to the git-grep this commit extracts into a helper. Carried into the helper rather than dropped; it is the CLAUDE.md rule for any git subprocess naming its target with `cmd.Dir`.
- `runner_gather_test.go` — `main` created this file for `TestGatherTrailsUsesNativeRepoBaseForFindings`. Both sets of tests kept, imports unioned.
- `setup_test.go` — append-vs-append with `TestConfigureCmd_SummarizeProvider_ExternalLocalTarget_GrantSurvives`. Both kept.

## Still open, deliberately not in here

`readCapped` opens with `osroot.OpenNoFollow`, and **this repo's own `AGENTS.md` is a symlink to `CLAUDE.md`** — so `entire runner tune` drops it. Harmless here because `CLAUDE.md` is read anyway, but a repo with only a symlinked `AGENTS.md` loses it. That is a product call (should the runner read symlinked docs at all?) rather than a fix to slip into a follow-up, and it predates these commits.

Two structural follow-ups also left out: making `OpenHookConfig` take a `HookConfigLocator`, which turns the guard test into a compile error but touches nine agent packages; and giving the registry a `ManagedWorktreePaths()` capability so "what does Entire write for this agent?" is the registry's question rather than three `switch agentName` blocks in `cli`.

## Verification

`mise run lint` 0 issues and `mise run test:ci` exit 0 on the rebased tree. The touched tests also run 5x together, because one of these commits fixed a `t.Parallel` test that called `osroot.ResetShared` and broke a different test — a single clean run does not catch that class.

content.text:
Yes — one finding, and it was a real bug I introduced. Fixed and pushed as `a8f907533`; CI is running.

**Copilot and the trail's own review independently flagged the same line**, `runner_gather.go:211`. I reproduced it rather than taking either at face value:

```
readCapped(dir, "go.mod", 1) over "\x80\x80..."
panic: runtime error: index out of range [-1]
```

The cause is squarely the `/simplify` pass. Swapping the whole-prefix `utf8.ValidString` for `utf8.RuneStart` at the cut was a 1000× win on paper, and I checked it produced identical cuts on the existing tests — but I missed that the change turned `cut` from a *slice bound* into a *subscript*. `s[:0]` is legal; `s[-1]` is not. The fixed iteration count was safe before and became an out-of-range index after.

The floor is now explicit — `max(0, maxLen-(utf8.UTFMax-1))` — rather than implied by a loop count, and a cut that finds no rune start stays at `maxLen` so the file's own bytes survive.

Two things worth noting about how this went:

No caller passes a cap anywhere near this small; the smallest is `go.mod`'s 400. So it was latent, and neither reviewer could show it firing in production. That's an argument for pinning it, not for shrugging — which is why the test sweeps caps 0–7 across three body shapes instead of just adding the one value Copilot named.

And my first draft of that test asserted "content is never empty", which **failed** — correctly. At `cap=1` over a two-byte rune, position 0 *is* a rune start, so `""` is the only valid-UTF-8 answer available. The test was wrong, not the code. It now asserts the actual contract: the cut either lands on a rune boundary or keeps the file's bytes.

That's three defects in this one function across the session — mid-rune cut, emptied file, now an underflow — each introduced while fixing the last. The function is eight lines. I've stopped optimising it.

`mise run lint` 0 issues, `test:ci` exit 0. The trail finding is resolved with the commit; PR #2290 still shows `REVIEW_REQUIRED` and needs a human approval, same as before.

CI came back red on my panic fix, and it was my fault again — a **Windows build failure**, not a test failure:

```
cmd\entire\cli\doctor_test.go:1779:20: undefined: syscall.Mkfifo
```

`syscall.Mkfifo` doesn't exist on Windows, so I guarded it the wrong way: `if runtime.GOOS == windowsGOOS { t.Skip(...) }` is a *runtime* check, and a runtime check still has to compile. The file never got that far. Moved to `doctor_fifo_unix_test.go` behind `//go:build unix`, which is the guard that actually applies. Pushed as `26e609ba8`; CI is running.

The part worth keeping: **`GOOS=windows go vet ./cmd/entire/cli/` reproduces it in one second**, and I never ran it. `mise run test:ci` compiles for the host only, so a clean local gate says nothing about Windows — and this branch changes `worktreedir`'s Windows path handling, which is precisely where I should have expected platform divergence. The whole tree now type-checks clean for windows, linux and darwin, and I've noted the command in the commit message.

Also note this broke *two* checks: the 3-second `test` job was the same build failure, not a separate problem.

To be straight about the pattern — that's now four defects of mine in this branch, three of them in eight lines of `readCapped` and each introduced while fixing the previous one, plus this build break in the test I added to pin the third. Every one was caught by a reviewer or by CI rather than by me. The one finding you asked about was real, and so was the fallout from fixing it.

Two things I'd suggest once CI is green: the memory note about verification should say "cross-compile for Windows when touching syscall or platform paths", and `readCapped` should be left alone.

Hit on 2026-09-07 (PR #2290). A test used `syscall.Mkfifo` guarded by `if runtime.GOOS == windowsGOOS { t.Skip(...) }`. Nine new findings from a fresh review. Seven fixed and pushed (`931c4e378`), two need your call. CI is running.

**The one worth your attention is a real hang, and it's pre-existing.** I reproduced it with this branch's binary in a repo where Entire isn't even enabled:

```
mkdir -p .claude && mkfifo .claude/settings.json && entire doctor
# prints "Metadata branches: OK", then blocks in openat forever
```

Stack sample confirms it: `osroot.OpenNoFollow` does a plain `parent.Open(leaf)` with no `O_NONBLOCK`, so opening a FIFO blocks. Every agent's config read goes through it. **Not mine** — my branch's only `osroot.go` change was an error-unwrap — but my new type check was gated on `prefix != name`, so the scan reported the condition *clean*. That half I fixed: both positions are now checked (directory above, regular file at the leaf), which also makes the branch's own "the leaf is refused too" claim true again.

Two bounding facts: only a FIFO hangs (a socket errors, a regular file and char device open fine), and git has no tree mode for a FIFO, so it can't arrive by clone — local action only. A footgun, not a vulnerability.

**Decision 1:** the actual fix is three lines in `OpenNoFollow` — it already `Lstat`s the leaf and checks for a symlink, so rejecting a non-regular type there costs nothing and covers all seven agents plus `permissions.go`. Want it in this PR, or filed as its own issue? The reviewer recommended filing separately to keep the re-land focused; I lean that way but it's a live hang either way.

**Decision 2:** the reviewer also observed that `readCapped`'s UTF-8 work has nothing to do with `os.Root` coverage and is a clean candidate for its own PR. That's true. I did **not** squash the three `readCapped` commits as suggested — they're non-contiguous (the cleanup commit sits between them), so reordering means an interactive rebase over files I've touched repeatedly, and force-pushing a reordered history is what lost this work the first time. Happy to do it if you want the tidier history.

Of the seven fixed, two were things I'd broken in the last two rounds: inserting `const claudeDirName` silently stole a 22-line doc block from `searchSkillTemplate`, and `skipWithoutSymlinks` became a *seventh* copy of the helper in the commit that removed six. The rest were a redundant return value, pi comments explaining #2220's change in the wrong file, and doc inaccuracies.

I also exported `paths.DescribeMode` rather than write a seventh mode-describing switch, so doctor's two scans now name the same conditions in the same words.

`lint` 0 issues, `test:ci` exit 0, and `GOOS=windows|linux|darwin go vet ./...` all clean — I'm running the cross-OS check every time now.

`readCapped` embeds repo docs (`CLAUDE.md`, `AGENTS.md`, `README.md`, `go.mod`) into the prompt `entire runner tune` sends to a model. Its cap is a byte budget applied as `s[:maxLen]`, while both callers describe it in characters:

```go
tuneDocCap    = 6000 // max chars embedded per doc (CLAUDE.md etc.)
tuneReadmeCap = 2000
```

A doc whose 6000th byte lands inside a multi-byte rune therefore put an invalid UTF-8 sequence into the prompt. Nothing downstream validates it, so it was invisible from the call site.

## The fix

A continuation byte at the cut is exactly what "we cut mid-rune" means, so back off the continuation bytes — at most `UTFMax-1` of them, the furthest a rune's start can be. `utf8.RuneStart` answers that from one byte.

Validating the prefix instead (`utf8.ValidString(s[:cut])`) answers a different question and is the wrong tool twice over: it walks the whole 6KB, and it returns false for a doc that is not UTF-8 *at all*, so chasing it back finds no valid prefix and drops the file's content in favour of a bare truncation marker. Invalidity our cut did not cause is the file's own, and the under-cap path already passes those bytes through.

## Two traps, both pinned by tests

Getting here took two wrong turns, and the tests exist so neither comes back:

- **An unbounded backoff empties a non-UTF-8 file.** A latin-1 README came back as nothing but `…(truncated)…` — worse than the mid-rune cut being fixed.
- **The floor has to be explicit, not implied by an iteration count.** At `maxLen=1` over a file of continuation bytes, a count-based bound indexes `s[-1]` and panics. Latent — the smallest cap any caller passes is `go.mod`'s 400 — which is the reason to pin it rather than shrug.

## Tests

These are the first tests `readCapped` has had: the boundary itself, a short file, a missing one, a non-UTF-8 doc keeping its content, and every cap from 0 to 7 across three body shapes.

The last one asserts the contract as a disjunction — the cut lands on a rune boundary, **or** it keeps the file's own bytes — rather than "not empty". An empty result is correct below one rune's width, where no non-empty valid prefix exists; an earlier draft of the test asserted non-empty and was wrong about the contract, not the code.

## Why it's separate

Split out of #2290 (os.Root coverage follow-ups) on review feedback: a byte cap cutting a rune in prompt text has nothing to do with filesystem anchoring, and this is the piece of that branch that stands alone. #2290 no longer touches `runner_gather.go`.

Here's the issue description to share:

**Title:** `A FIFO at an agent config path hangs every command that reads it`

> `entire doctor` — and any command that reads an agent's hook config — blocks indefinitely if a named pipe sits at the config path. In a repo where Entire isn't even enabled:
>
> ```
> mkdir -p .claude && mkfifo .claude/settings.json
> entire doctor
> # prints "✓ Metadata branches: OK", then blocks in openat. Ctrl-C only.
> ```
>
> `osroot.OpenNoFollow` (`cmd/entire/cli/osroot/osroot.go:80`) opens the leaf with a plain `parent.Open(leaf)` and no `O_NONBLOCK`, so `open(2)` on a FIFO waits for a writer that never comes:
>
> ```
> os.(*Root).Open                 root.go:103
> osroot.OpenNoFollow             osroot/osroot.go:80
> agent.(*HookConfigFile).Read    agent/hook_config_file.go:112
> claudecode.loadClaudeSettings   claudecode/hooks.go:433
> ```
>
> All seven worktree-config agents share the shape (cursor, copilotcli, geminicli, factoryaidroid, opencode, pi), plus `permissions.go`.
>
> **Two things that bound it.** Only a FIFO hangs — a socket fails with "operation not supported on socket", and a regular file or char device opens fine. And git has no tree mode for a FIFO, so it cannot arrive by clone: this needs local action. It's a liveness footgun, not the traversal class the anchor work defends against.
>
> **Suggested fix:** `OpenNoFollow` already `Lstat`s the leaf to reject a symlink, so rejecting a non-regular type in the same place costs nothing and covers every caller.
>
> PR #2290 makes the condition *reportable* — `entire doctor` now names a wrong-typed config path instead of passing it as clean — but a scan can't prevent the hang.
